title: The Breeder's Son

where.detail: his father's upper paddock, the gate open onto the hill

time: a spring in his boyhood, twenty years before the Steps
last_beat: His father took the gate by the top bar, swung it open onto the hill and stood aside from it, and Darrow rode the bay out through it.

people.did: Got onto the bay nobody could sit by never being where it expected him, and rode it out through the gate his father opened.

facts.fact: As a boy of eleven he had walked at a horse's head since before he could argue, the way a horse-breeder's son is raised in the Edgemoor hills.
He got onto the bay by going sideways into the place it had just left instead of backward, and up the rail to be higher than its eye.
His father, who said nothing about most things, opened the gate for him without a word.
facts.evidence: as he said nothing about most things

title: His Own

where.detail: the Holloway below the Edgemoor hill road at dusk, at the back of the Ninth's string

time: autumn, the year he was sixteen; the years before the Ninth was his
last_beat: He walked at the mare's head down the Holloway at dusk behind the Ninth's string, and kept his hand under her jaw past the first stone, where he had leave, and past the second, which was his own.

people.did: Rode his father's long grey mare down off the hill to a Lowmarch muster, led her through the levy's billhooks untouched, told the Ninth's sergeant he was his own son, and walked at her head down the Holloway behind the Ninth's string.

facts.fact: At sixteen he rode the long grey mare down off the Edgemoor hills to a Lowmarch muster, with his father's brand on her and his father's word that the horse was his.
facts.evidence: "She's yours," his father said. "The brand's mine.

facts.fact: He named the grey filly out of the mare Thistle, for standing in the thistles at the top of the far field to be let alone.
facts.evidence: He had named her Thistle for it the spring before

facts.fact: He led the mare through a line of forty levy boys and their billhooks by watching their shoulders rather than the steel, and came out with every hair of her untouched.
facts.evidence: He watched their shoulders, not the steel.

facts.fact: Asked by the Ninth's sergeant whose son he was, he answered that he was his own.
He went down the Holloway at dusk at the back of the Ninth's string, on his feet, with his hand under the mare's jaw.
facts.evidence: He walked at her head with his hand under her jaw

codex.name: Thistle
codex.text: A grey filly out of the long grey mare of Darrow's father's, who stood in the thistles at the top of the far field to be let alone; Darrow named her for it the spring before he was sixteen, and his father let the name go by (Tale 1, Piece 2).

codex.name: The Lowmarch muster
codex.text: On a green below the Edgemoor hill road, where the Holloway goes through: levy boys with billhooks counted by the bell-house clerk, a string of hill greys for the lances to look over, and the lance's own horses picketed beyond the bell-house. At sixteen Darrow led his mare through the levy's line without a hook touching her, and the Ninth's sergeant let him walk her at the back of the string as far as the fifth milestone (Tale 1, Piece 2).
